definition: Obfuscate means to make something deliberately hard to understand.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word obfuscate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know obfuscate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The professor accused the textbook of obfuscating: a rule any coach could teach in a minute took the authors nine symbol-choked pages.
Blur is far milder than obfuscate — a blurred explanation softens the edges of one detail, often by accident.
Muddle stops short of obfuscate: a muddled speaker confuses you without meaning to, while an obfuscating one builds the fog on purpose.

Muddy is the informal cousin of obfuscate — stirring silt into water that was clear a moment ago. Anyone can muddy an issue with one careless sentence; to obfuscate is to build the fog deliberately and at length, under jargon and digressions. Muddy belongs to the kitchen table, obfuscate to the courtroom.

To befog is to wrap a subject in mist rather than burying it — the outline stays visible, just softened. Obfuscate goes further: it piles on jargon, digressions, and qualifications until no picture forms at all, and it always accuses the fog-maker of acting on purpose.

The root fuscus, 'dark,' arrived in English inside obfuscate and stayed there — no everyday English word shares it. The prefix ob-, 'over, completely,' is everywhere, but the darkness at the heart of this word has no living relatives.

When the collector asked where the atlas had been acquired, the dealer obfuscated — an anecdote about Lisbon, a digression on paper mills, a name that changed twice — until closing time arrived with the question still standing.
Obfuscate is deliberate fog.

Blurring softens a detail, and muddling confuses by accident; to obfuscate is to bury the clear thing on purpose — under jargon, digressions, and qualifications — so that pursuit gives up before it arrives.
Obfuscate is an accusation of intent — it says the fog was manufactured.
Confusing writing may earn 'muddled'; only writing meant to defeat the reader earns obfuscate.
Its unit-mates divide the territory: misrepresent plants a false picture, while obfuscate makes sure no picture forms at all.
